skill.name: role-creator
skill.description: Create Codex custom agent roles by collecting required inputs, generating role TOML files, installing declarations, and validating supported keys.
skill.summary: Create, install, and validate Codex custom agent role configurations.
skill.author: am-will

security_audit.summary: Most high static findings are false positives from Markdown code spans, example paths, and placeholder environment variable names. Confirmed risks involve persistent Codex config modification, arbitrary developer-instructions file ingestion, MCP name config injection, and arbitrary role config output paths. No prompt injection attempt was found in the reviewed skill files.

remediation.suggestion: Add a dry-run mode, show the exact target config path, and require explicit confirmation before writing global config files.
Reject sensitive paths, prefer workspace-relative files, and display the resolved file path before reading it into a role config.
Validate MCP names with a strict identifier pattern or pass names to tomlq as data instead of concatenating them into the filter.
Resolve and display output paths, refuse existing files unless update is confirmed, and restrict default writes to a role config directory.
Require a separate confirmation for danger-full-access, network access, live search, shell tools, MCP commands, and environment variable wiring.

semantic_findings.title: Unsafe MCP Name Interpolation
semantic_findings.description: The script trims MCP names from user input and embeds them directly into a generated tomlq filter. A crafted MCP name containing quote or filter syntax can alter the generated role config beyond the requested enable or disable change.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The MCP names are parsed from user-controlled CSV input and concatenated into the filter string instead of being passed as data. This is a clear config-injection risk, though it does not directly execute shell commands.

semantic_findings.title: Arbitrary Role Config Output Path
semantic_findings.description: The writer script creates the parent directory for the supplied output path and writes generated TOML directly to that path. A mistaken or malicious path can overwrite any file the caller can write.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The output path is fully user supplied, mkdir creates its parent directory, and the redirection overwrites the target file. The skill asks for confirmation, but the script has no path guard.

semantic_findings.title: Privilege-Expanding Role Options
semantic_findings.description: The skill can generate role configs that enable danger-full-access, network access, web search, shell tools, MCP commands, and MCP environment variable wiring. These options are user-gated, but installed roles can materially change subagent permissions and external access.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The files explicitly list unrestricted sandboxing, network/search controls, shell tooling, MCP commands, and environment variable names. The documentation requires explicit requests, which limits but does not remove the risk.

content.value_statement: Custom Codex roles require exact TOML keys and careful installation. This skill guides inputs, writes role config files, installs declarations, and validates supported keys.
actual_capabilities: Collects required role inputs before writing configuration files.
Generates minimal Codex role config files with model, reasoning effort, and developer instructions.
Installs role declarations into global or project Codex config files.
Provides templates for restricted, frontend, and full-surface role profiles.
Validates agent declaration keys and role config top-level keys against a schema.
limitations: Requires local jq, tomlq, and the Codex config schema for validation.
Can overwrite files when given an incorrect output path.
Does not verify that generated developer instructions are secure or complete.
Advanced sandbox, network, MCP, and search settings require user review.

use_cases.title: Create a Research Role
use_cases.description: Build a reusable Codex role that reads code and reports file evidence without editing files.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Roles
use_cases.description: Create consistent role templates with required fields, descriptions, and validation steps.

use_cases.title: Install Project Subagents
use_cases.description: Register project-scoped agents with explicit sandbox, search, and MCP choices.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Role
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for one global role.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a global Codex researcher role with medium reasoning. Keep optional settings inherited and ask before writing files.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Project Role
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a project-scoped implementation role for this repository. Use high reasoning and validate the role before reporting success.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Restricted Role
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a read-focused audit role with web search disabled, no network access, and workspace-write sandboxing.

prompt_templates.title: Design an Advanced Template
prompt_templates.scenario: Expert setup using optional role controls.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a reusable role template with MCP enable flags, schema validation, and a clear list of inherited settings.

output_examples.output: The skill asks for model, reasoning, scope, role name, description, and config path, then prepares a minimal role profile.
It registers the role declaration, enables multi-agent support, creates a backup, and reports the selected config path.
It checks required fields, allowed declaration keys, and schema-supported top-level config keys.

best_practices: Use project-scoped roles when a role only applies to one repository.
Keep role configs minimal unless a user explicitly requests extra permissions.
Run validation after every install or update before using the role.
anti_patterns: Do not install global roles without confirming the target config file.
Do not enable danger-full-access, network access, or MCP servers by default.
Do not paste secrets into developer instructions or role templates.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates Codex role config files and registers agent declarations in a Codex config file.

faq.question: Can it install roles globally?
faq.answer: Yes. It can target the global Codex config or a project config after scope confirmation.

faq.question: Does it validate the result?
faq.answer: Yes. The validation script checks required fields, declaration keys, and supported top-level role config keys.

faq.question: Can it configure sandboxing?
faq.answer: Yes. It supports sandbox options only when the user explicitly requests them.

faq.question: Does it manage MCP servers?
faq.answer: It can enable, disable, or clear MCP server entries in generated role config files.

faq.question: What tools does it require?
faq.answer: The scripts expect bash, jq, tomlq, and access to the Codex config schema for validation.
